sampling_model.design: For fixed-law supporting results, regular samples jointly identify \(p\), \(r\), and \(\mu\). For uniform questions, row \(n\) contains independent observations from \(P_n^\circ\), with fixed finite supports and cell-probability floors indexed by \(\kappa_n\). The response-boundary counterexample uses uniform \(2\times2\) response-study cells, fixed deployment margins, and Bernoulli means \(\lambda/n\), so its obstruction is collapsing response variance rather than rare deployment or study cells.
sampling_model.units: Target contexts and actions are multinomial draws; separate interventional response units identify every finite \((c,x)\) cell. Dependence across stacked regular components is allowed through a declared row influence vector. In the singleton counterexample the margins are observed without error and only the four response means are sampled.
sampling_model.treatment: The response study observes micro action \(X\); target macro action \(h\) uses an unknown context-only selector calibrated to \(r\). The response-boundary theorem changes only the sampling law for the identified micro-response means and does not alter the causal selector class or target interval.
sampling_model.overlap: The class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) imposes floors on \(p_n\), \(r_n\), and \(\pi_n\), but no lower bound on Bernoulli response means, endpoint-relevant variances, or Gaussian anti-concentration. Consequently it contains the singleton response-boundary array even for a floor sequence satisfying \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\). The repaired uniform question must add a faithful response regularity condition before imposing any margin or tuning rates.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The stacked estimator and multiplier obey the assumed absolute bounded-Lipschitz approximations. The singleton theorem shows that these approximations can both converge to a degenerate Gaussian law while the all-zero sample event retains positive limiting probability, the multiplier critical value is zero, and the ridged endpoint estimate misses the true singleton interval. Uniform inference therefore needs response-side relative variance or anti-concentration control beyond the two existing approximation assumptions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Specified version-assignment laws identify overall multiple-version effects.
Section 2.1.1, Theorem 1, Equation (4), gives a constructive sharp identified set for partially linear coefficients from unlinked outcome and covariate margins.
Causal consistency requires intervention behavior to commute across related structural models.
Constructive causal abstractions relate low-level and high-level models through state and intervention maps.
Proposition 1 and Definition 6 give the all-intervention partial-projection condition, while Equation 11 fixes a canonical residual conditional law for a fixed low-level SCM and abstraction map.
The COTA objective is jointly convex in causally constrained transport plans.
Estimated measures and costs produce optimal-face transport limits.
Parametric optimization theory gives directional expansions of optimal values under nonunique solution and multiplier sets.
Danskin's envelope theorem expresses directional derivatives through the optimizing set.
The numerical delta method consistently estimates directionally differentiable limit laws with a slowly vanishing step.
Derivative-based resampling restores inference for directionally differentiable maps when the ordinary bootstrap fails.
The linear-program value procedure has a delta-conditioned uniform-consistency guarantee under optimizer multiplicity.
PDX precision strategies are compared with clinically meaningful controls under known recommendation rules.

Methodology, Theorem 3.2, gives uniformly valid confidence sets for linear functionals defined by linear moment inequalities by bootstrapping fixed, randomly perturbed linear-program value functions; coverage over the exact identified set tends to one and exact coverage is obtained on an outer perturbed set.

Main Results, Theorem 3, gives uniformly valid confidence sets for sharp scalar projections of finite affine identified sets under uniform positive rank, slack, and moment constants, allowing multiplicity of primal optima.

body.tldr: The selector envelope and its fixed-law directional inference remain established supporting results, but the proposed rare-margin rate window is not sufficient on the unrepaired triangular-array class. A new schedule-independent response-boundary theorem constructs a singleton experiment class on which both uniform bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations hold while simultaneous coverage is at most \(1-e^{-\lambda}<1-\alpha\). The uniform frontier must therefore begin by imposing a faithful response-interiority, nondegenerate-variance, relative variance-consistency, or anti-concentration condition; only then is the sufficiency or sharpness of \(n\kappa_n^3\) a meaningful open question.

project_justification.gap: Cho--Russell and Gafarov provide uniform LP inference under different perturbation, regularization, and fixed-regularity frameworks. For the row-feasible paired numerical-delta procedure, the present theorem additionally shows that absolute bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximation is inadequate when response variance collapses. Existing comparisons therefore do not supply either the missing response regularity condition or the rare-margin face-switching analysis on the repaired class.
project_justification.niche: The remaining field-level niche has two ordered parts: first characterize a primitive and noncircular response regularity condition sufficient for uniform critical-value behavior; then determine the procedure-specific shrinking-margin boundary and tuning window under that condition. The proved singleton theorem is a negative prerequisite result, not a sharp rare-margin threshold.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit all-zero response construction and the singleton class \(\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\), proves that both bounded-Lipschitz approximation suprema reduce to discrepancies that vanish on this class, and nevertheless proves schedule-independent undercoverage. It then reformulates the uniform sufficiency question on a to-be-specified response-regular subclass before asking whether \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\), \((n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n)\), and \(t_n=o(\kappa_n)\) suffice.

body.related_work: VanderWeele and Hernán show that multiple-version effects depend on a specified version-assignment distribution. Béal and Latouche apply that setup to PDX precision-medicine comparisons. D'Haultfoeuille, Gaillac, and Maurel, Section 2.1.1, Theorem 1 and Equation (4), characterize a sharp coefficient set under unlinked margins through transport; that result informs the discrete selector envelope. Rubenstein et al. and Beckers and Halpern inform the intervention and abstraction semantics. Xia and Bareinboim, Proposition 1 and Definition 6, supply the partial-projection condition instantiated by the semantic lemma; their Equation 11 canonical residual law is fixed and cannot span a positive-dimensional free-selector polytope. Felekis et al. inform the transport representation. Bonnans and Shapiro and Danskin directly supply the parametric linear-program sensitivity tools, while Hundrieser et al. study estimated-cost transport. Fang and Santos provide the general directional-inference framework, and Hong and Li supply the fixed-law numerical-delta corollary. Cho and Russell, Methodology, Theorem 3.2, obtain uniform inference for linear functionals defined by linear moment inequalities by bootstrapping randomly perturbed LP values. Their perturbation support is fixed and nonvanishing, and their procedure differs from the present row-feasible numerical delta. Gafarov, Main Results, Theorem 3, constructs uniformly valid confidence sets for sharp affine identified-set projections, including flat primal faces, by regularized support functions under uniform positive rank and slack constants. Voronin provides delta-conditioned uniform consistency and pointwise inference for an LP-value procedure. None of these comparator results turns absolute bounded-Lipschitz approximation into coverage at a collapsing response-variance boundary. The new singleton theorem isolates that missing prerequisite; the rare-margin rate boundary remains open only after an appropriate response-regular class is specified.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The selector seed \(S\) is atomless even though all endogenous and response domains are finite. The residual coordinate is endogenous with equation \(Z_s=g_s(C,S)\), which is essential for interventions on \(C\) to commute; its induced conditional law varies with \(s\). The result proves the Xia--Bareinboim Definition-6 partial-projection identity selector by selector and does not preserve one fixed canonical Equation-11 residual law or one common canonical Layer-3 map across distinct selectors.
body.honest_scope: The paper proves a schedule-independent failure theorem for the specific paired numerical-delta confidence envelope on one collapsing-response singleton class. It does not prove a minimax impossibility for other confidence procedures and does not establish a sharp threshold in \(n\kappa_n^3\). The sufficient-regime and procedural-sharpness questions remain open on a repaired class whose additional response-interiority, nondegenerate-variance, relative variance-consistency, or anti-concentration condition must still be formulated without assuming coverage. The experiment class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) itself has only margin and response-study cell floors. Cho--Russell and Gafarov already provide uniform LP inference using different constructions and regularity classes. The projected SCM construction, sharp selector image, endpoint certificates, fixed-map obstruction, cycle criterion, fixed-interior derivative, and pointwise numerical-delta result retain their supporting scope.
body.interpretation: For deployment analyses, fixed-support pointwise inference remains available at an interior law, including nonunique transport faces. A triangular-array claim that permits identified Bernoulli response means to approach zero requires more: good absolute Gaussian and multiplier approximation can coexist with a positive-probability all-zero study and severe undercoverage. Practitioners should therefore diagnose response-side effective information and variance calibration before applying a rare-margin numerical-step rule.
